title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the PD de Rham notes. It is a typescript page (p. 46 of Exposé IX) of Grothendieck's 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie', SGA 7 I, Exposé IX, §4.5–4.6, misfiled in cote 136. The neighbouring pages are handwritten PD-algebra computations with no relation to it.

Setting: V is a discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue characteristic p. A_K is an abelian variety over K, ℓ ≠ p is a prime, and U_ℓ = T_ℓ(A(K̄)) is the ℓ-adic Tate module.

The Swan conductor of a Galois module F_K killed by ℓ is defined by choosing a finite quotient Γ of inertia through which the action factors (a choice depending a priori on ℓ). One then sets α_s(F_K) = length of Hom_{Z_ℓ[Γ]}(Sw, F). Here Sw is the Swan module, a projective Z_ℓ[Γ]-module. Because Sw is projective, α_s is additive in exact sequences.

Applied to F = _ℓA_K, the ℓ-torsion, this gives (4.5.4): α_s(A_K; ℓ) = length Hom_{Z_ℓ(Γ)}(Sw, U_ℓ ⊗ F_ℓ). This integer is called the wild ('immodéré', 'sauvage') conductor exponent. It is defined for any V by passing to the henselisation, and one reduces at once to S strictly local.

Corollary 4.6 states that this exponent does not depend on ℓ ≠ p.

The proof begins on this page. One computes Hom(L, U_ℓ ⊗ F_ℓ) for an arbitrary projective Z_ℓ[Γ]-module L. The filtration (4.1.1) of U_ℓ consists of fixed part ⊂ orthogonal of fixed part, i.e. toric/abelian/unipotent layers. Its pieces are Z_ℓ-direct summands, so the computation can be done on the graded pieces. On the outer pieces wild inertia acts trivially. The middle piece is the Tate module of an abelian variety with potentially good reduction. For that piece, independence of ℓ follows from the integrality and ℓ-independence of the character of the finite inertia action (Serre–Tate).

The footnote defines further invariants:
- The tame conductor exponent is the drop in F_ℓ-dimension of _ℓA° between the geometric generic and special fibres. It equals 2λ+μ in the notation of (1.1.11): λ is presumably the unipotent rank and μ the toric rank, consistent with tame conductor = t + 2u.
- The total conductor is the sum of the tame and wild exponents. It is the local term in the Euler–Poincaré formula of SGA 5 X 6.2.
errors: No mathematical errors visible. 'manisfestement' is a typo in the original typescript.
